record.original_question: Let f be a multiplicative arithmetic function with property P, meaning that f(p^alpha) depends only on the exponent alpha and not on the prime p. Suppose f(p^alpha) grows like the divisor function value alpha + 1, but the ratio log f(p^2) / log f(p) is a Liouville number. If Q_f(X) denotes the number of f-champion numbers N <= X, where an integer N is f-champion when every M < N has f(M) < f(N), must there exist a constant c_f such that Q_f(X) = O((log X)^c_f) as X grows?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call an arithmetic function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ multiplicative if $f(1)=1$ and $f(mn)=f(m)f(n)$ whenever $\gcd(m,n)=1$. Say that $f$ has property (P) if for every prime $p$ and every integer $\alpha\ge 1$ the value $f(p^\alpha)$ depends only on $\alpha$ and not on $p$; in that case write $f(p^\alpha)=g(\alpha)$ for a fixed function $g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ with $g(0)=1$.

Assume that $f$ has property (P) and that the associated function $g$ satisfies the following two conditions:
(i) $g(\alpha)$ grows like the divisor-function value $\alpha+1$, in the sense that there exist constants $0<c_1\le c_2$ with $c_1(\alpha+1)\le g(\alpha)\le c_2(\alpha+1)$ for all $\alpha\ge 1$;
(ii) the ratio $\dfrac{\log g(2)}{\log g(1)}$ is a Liouville number (i.e. an irrational $\xi$ such that for every $n\ge 1$ there exist integers $p,q$ with $q>1$ and $0<|\xi-p/q|<q^{-n}$).

Call a positive integer $N$ an $f$-champion if $f(M)<f(N)$ for every positive integer $M<N$. Let 
$$Q_f(X)=\#\{N\le X : N\text{ is an }f\text{-champion}\}.$$

Must there necessarily exist a constant $c_f>0$ such that 
$$Q_f(X)=O\bigl((\log X)^{c_f}\bigr)\qquad\text{as }X\to\infty\,?$$

The problem is stated as not known in the source from which it is drawn, and no subsequent work confirming a polylogarithmic bound or a counterexample was located.
